questions.prompt: Match each kingdom to an example.
questions.explain: Five kingdoms, from tiny bacteria to giant trees.

questions.prompt: Which vertebrate class does each animal belong to?
questions.explain: Bats and dolphins are mammals: fur/hair, and milk for their young.

questions.prompt: Why is a mushroom NOT a plant?
options: It cannot make its own food by photosynthesis; it absorbs food from dead matter
It grows in the dark sometimes

questions.explain: Invertebrates, like insects and worms, have no backbone.

questions.prompt: The tiger's scientific name is Panthera tigris. What is ‘Panthera’?
options: Its genus (a group of closely related species)
questions.explain: Binomial names give the genus then the species, e.g. Panthera leo is the lion.

questions.prompt: A student says, “A bat flies and has wings, so it must be a bird.” Use evidence to explain why the bat is classified as a mammal.
questions.modelAnswer: Classification is based on many shared features, not one. Bats have fur (not feathers), give birth to live young and feed them on milk, and have no beak. These are features of mammals. Wings evolved separately in bats and birds, so flying alone doesn't make an animal a bird.
rubric: Explains why flight alone is not enough
questions.explain: Criterion C: justify a classification with evidence.
